request: Hi , Please create a filling system on the radiator , including a pouring section and a cap.

actions.operation: Create/add a filling system interface feature on the radiator (filler/pouring section)

parameters.placement: Top tank, near longitudinal mid-span (between the two fan bays) and centered left/right (z≈0 symmetry mid-plane).
parameters.axis_direction: Normal to top tank outer plane (positive y direction).
parameters.neck_outer_diameter: TBD (typical radiator filler neck range ~30-45 mm OD; confirm packaging/cap standard).
parameters.neck_inner_diameter: TBD (set by required fill flow and cap standard).
parameters.neck_height_above_top_tank: TBD (ensure hand clearance above top tank and fan shroud).
parameters.seal_seat_type: TBD (flat gasket land or conical seat depending on cap type).
parameters.cap_interface_type: TBD (thread or bayonet; most automotive radiator caps use bayonet lugs).
parameters.wall_thickness: TBD (consistent with tank material/process; ensure pressure integrity).

actions.relational_constraint: Located on the radiator; functionally must connect into the top tank/header volume for filling/bleeding; positioned at the topmost practical location for trapped-air purge.
actions.unresolved_reference: Although a filler/cap boss is already present in the current model (visible in multiview and listed as S4 filler/cap surface), confirm whether the request is to (a) newly create from scratch, (b) resize/standardize the existing neck to a specified cap standard, or (c) relocate it. Also confirm neck/cap standard and key diameters/heights.
steps: Assessment / interaction choice: The multiview images and model.json indicate an existing filler neck/cap boss on the top tank (Section S4, major face 0012 / Brep FACE 798). Therefore, treat this action primarily as: (1) validate/standardize the existing pouring neck geometry and (2) ensure a true opening into the tank exists (cut) and a proper seal seat/interface is modeled. If the existing boss is only cosmetic, replace it with a parametric filler neck feature built from the top plane (0011).

Set datum and placement: Use the Top tank outer plane (face_code 0011, Brep_id FACE 46, y≈174.852) as the primary sketch plane. Create/confirm a construction point at the intended neck center: centered between the fan bays (use assembly mid-plane z≈0 as reference) and positioned on the top tank mid-width. If needed, project/measure from visible midline between fans (Section S8 divider region) to place the neck at the true midpoint.

Create the pouring opening into the tank: On plane 0011, sketch a circle for the neck bore (ID = neck_inner_diameter). Perform an Extrude-Cut (or Hole feature) normal to the plane, cutting through the top tank wall into the interior volume. Terminate condition: 'Up to Next' / 'Up to Face' into the internal cavity (do not cut through the opposite wall). This step ensures the filler is functional rather than only a surface boss.

Create the neck outer wall: On the same plane 0011 (or on the cut edge as a sketch reference), sketch concentric circles for neck OD (neck_outer_diameter) and optionally an outer reinforcement flange OD (TBD). Extrude-Boss upward (+y) to neck_height_above_top_tank. If the current boss surface 0012 exists and is to be kept, use it as a reference and adjust by direct-edit/replace-face to match the new parametric profile; otherwise, suppress/remove the cosmetic boss and rebuild as solid features.

Add cap interface features (pouring section interface): Depending on cap_interface_type: (A) Bayonet: create two opposing lug ramps/ears near the neck top—sketch lug profiles on a plane normal to the neck axis, then extrude-boss outward; add draft/helix-like ramp via sweep or draft to provide locking rotation. (B) Thread: create an external thread by helical sweep or cosmetic thread (if detailed thread not required), ensuring major/minor diameters match chosen cap standard.

Add seal seat and lead-in: Create a flat gasket land or conical seat at the top of the neck (per seal_seat_type). Add a small chamfer (e.g., 0.5–1.5 mm TBD) to the bore entry to ease pouring and cap installation. Add fillets/blends at the neck-to-tank transition for stress reduction and manufacturability (radius TBD).

Check clearances and function: Verify the neck/cap envelope clears nearby geometry visible in multiview (fan shrouds on the fan side, Sections S6/S7, and the top tank perimeter). Ensure the opening is at the highest point of the top tank for filling/air purge and does not intersect internal structures.

actions.operation: Create/add a cap for the filling system

parameters.cap_component: TBD (separate part/component recommended for assembly realism; can also be modeled as a simplified closed state).
parameters.cap_outer_diameter: TBD (must provide hand grip; typically larger than neck OD).
parameters.cap_height: TBD (includes grip and internal engagement depth).
parameters.engagement_type: Match neck interface: bayonet lugs or internal thread.
parameters.seal_feature: TBD (gasket/washer groove or molded seal lip).
parameters.pressure_relief_detail: Optional/TBD (usually present in real radiator caps; can be simplified/omitted).

actions.relational_constraint: Cap mates with and closes the pouring section; must be concentric with filler neck axis and seat against the seal land/seat on the neck.
actions.unresolved_reference: Confirm whether the cap needs to be modeled as a detailed pressure cap (with spring/valves) or as an exterior-only simplified cap. Confirm the chosen interface standard (bayonet vs thread) so the internal engagement features match the neck.
steps: Decide modeling strategy: Create the cap as a NEW component/body so it can be shown assembled/disassembled and so it does not boolean-merge into the tank. Use the neck axis (from the pouring section created/standardized on S4) as the primary reference.

Create cap base sketch plane: Create a plane coincident with the top of the neck seal seat (or offset from top tank plane 0011 by neck_height_above_top_tank). Ensure plane normal aligns with the neck axis (+y).

Model the cap exterior: Sketch a cap cross-section (outer wall, top dome/flat, grip ribs) and Revolve 360° about the neck axis to form the main cap body. If a non-round grip is preferred (e.g., wings), instead extrude a profile and blend; but a revolve is the most robust baseline.

Model internal engagement: (A) Bayonet cap: create internal slots and ramps matching the neck’s bayonet lugs—sketch slot profiles on an internal cylindrical face and perform Extrude-Cut; add ramp via sweep/draft. (B) Threaded cap: create internal thread by helical sweep cut or apply cosmetic thread if simplified.

Add sealing feature: Create an internal gasket groove or an annular sealing lip that contacts the neck’s seal seat. Use fillets/chamfers to avoid sharp edges at the sealing interface. Ensure the cap bottoms out on the designed seat rather than on unintended surfaces.

Assemble/mate position: Constrain the cap concentrically to the neck and set the seated position with a coincident/offset mate at the seal seat. If showing a locked position, apply an angular rotation corresponding to bayonet lock travel (TBD).
Visual/functional checks: Verify the cap clears the top tank edges and any nearby hose interfaces. Confirm there is sufficient external grip area above the top tank for manual removal.

intention: Provide a way to fill the radiator (pour coolant/working fluid into it) and close/seal the opening with a cap.

Standardize/ensure the existing top filler neck/cap region on the top tank is a functional opening into the tank with an appropriate sealing and retention interface, consistent with typical radiator serviceability and packaging.
